extracted.intended_audience: journal production staff, XML/prepress suppliers, publishers, and typesetters implementing JATS + CRediT metadata
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for marking up and displaying author contribution information (CRediT roles and free-text Author Contributions statements) in JATS XML and in typeset backmatter; includes tagging attributes, placement rules, degree-of-contribution handling, and compatibility with older JATS versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of CRediT roles and Author Contributions statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles may include CRediT roles and/or a free text Author Contributions statement to describe the activities of each person who contributed to the article. CRediT roles and Author Contributions statement are optional components that should be tagged if available for an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CRediT information is provided for an article (typically transmitted in article metadata), the CRediT roles for each author should be tagged using the <role> element within <contrib> as part of the article metadata. Free-text Author Contributions statements should be placed in backmatter (either as their own <sec sec-type="author-contributions"> or inside <ack>).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagging CRediT roles in metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The <role> element should be used within the <contrib> element to tag the CRediT roles that are assigned to the contributors (authors) on the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each <role> element should have the name of the CRediT role as text and include attributes @vocab, @vocab-identifier, @vocab-term, and @vocab-term-identifier that correspond to the CRediT role (pointing to credit.niso.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attributes for tagged CRediT roles (JATS 1.2+)
rubrics_metrics.description: When tagging CRediT roles, include machine-readable vocabulary attributes linking the role to the CRediT taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @vocab="credit" and set @vocab-identifier and @vocab-term-identifier to the appropriate credit.niso.org URIs so roles are unambiguously identified in metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of CRediT roles in typeset backmatter
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT roles should be displayed in typeset PDFs as a backmatter section titled 'Author Contributions' and formatted according to the Interact template guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not duplicate CRediT roles within the article XML purely to create display; if roles are present in metadata they should be displayed following the Interact template guide. Example: list each author followed by their CRediT roles formatted in one line per author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not duplicate CRediT metadata and backmatter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally, CRediT information should not be duplicated within an article because any inconsistencies may require input from the authors to resolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If roles are present in the article metadata and the Author Contributions statement is present as free text, avoid duplicating role lists in XML backmatter; reconcile inconsistencies via an author query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of free-text Author Contributions statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An Author Contributions Statement may be included as its own section or as part of the acknowledgements and should be placed in the back of an article (within <back>) before the references list.

rubrics_metrics.name: If both CRediT metadata and free-text statements are present
rubrics_metrics.description: If both CRediT roles and a free text Author Contributions statement are present, manage placement and queries carefully to avoid inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the free-text Author Contributions statement in the Acknowledgements section and raise an author query to resolve potential inconsistencies between metadata and free text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributors not listed as authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors who are not included in the author list cannot have CRediT roles tagged using <role> elements in article metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the contributions of non-author contributors in the Author Contribution Statement or acknowledgements instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple roles per contributor
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contributor has more than one role then separate <role> elements should be used within the <contrib> element to hold each of the contributor’s roles individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show multiple <role> elements nested under a single <contrib> to represent multiple CRediT roles for a single author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other (non-CRediT) uses of the <role> element
rubrics_metrics.description: The <role> element can also hold non-CRediT roles for a contributor (e.g., 'Reviewing Editor', 'PhD Student', pronouns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contributors have both CRediT and non-CRediT roles use separate <role> elements. Distinguish CRediT roles by checking the @vocab or the URIs in the @vocab-term-identifier/@vocab-identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying CRediT roles vs other roles
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT <role> elements can be distinguished from <role> elements that contain other kinds of roles programmatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether 'credit.niso.org' is contained within the @vocab-term-identifier or @content-type attributes, or whether the @vocab attribute equals 'credit' to determine that a <role> is a CRediT role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of contribution values and display
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one contributor has the same CRediT role, each contributor’s degree of contribution may optionally be specified as 'equal', 'lead', or 'supporting'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a degree is provided, the degree should be displayed in parenthesis after the CRediT role in the text of the <role> element and the <role> element should have a @degree-contribution attribute with value 'equal', 'lead', or 'supporting'. Example: degree-contribution="equal" and text 'Writing – original draft (equal)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography of role names (dash character)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dash in 'Writing – original draft' and 'Writing – review & editing' is an en dash (–) rather than a hyphen (-).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the en dash character in displayed role names to match the recommended typographic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepress suppliers and extraction from free-text
rubrics_metrics.description: Although free text Author Contributions statements may contain recognizable CRediT roles, extracting structured CRediT metadata from free text is not generally expected of prepress suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraction from free text is possible in clear cases but is not scalable because of variability and ambiguity; instructions will be given only if extraction is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ambiguous abbreviated contributor naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Using only initials for contributors in Author Contributions Statements is concise but can introduce ambiguity if two authors have the same initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer full names (or sufficiently disambiguating forms) in Author Contributions statements to avoid ambiguity when extracting or matching CRediT roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct tagging of Author Contributions section (required attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author Contributions section should include sec-type attribute when used as a standalone section in backmatter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an Author Contributions Statement is in its own section, add @sec-type="author-contributions" on the <sec> element. Omitting @sec-type is incorrect (example shows a correction adding sec-type).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including submission form text in published Author Contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Text from submission forms (e.g., 'Please provide…') should not be included in the published Author Contributions statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove submission-form prompts and only publish the actual author-provided statement; raising an author query may be necessary to clean up content.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Conceptualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas; formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag as <role vocab='credit' ...>Conceptualization</role> with appropriate credit.niso.org URIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Data curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later re-use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag as Data curation and include in contributor <contrib> metadata if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Formal analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyse or synthesize study data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag as Formal analysis with corresponding vocab URIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Funding acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag as Funding acquisition and place in metadata for contributors who secured funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag contributors who performed experiments, fieldwork, or data collection as Investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Development or design of methodology; creation of models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Methodology to credit contributors who designed methods or models.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Project administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Project administration to those with management/coordination responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag contributors who provided materials or tools as Resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Software for contributors who developed or implemented code or algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Supervision to PIs or team leads who provided leadership and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Validation to credit work that confirms reproducibility/verification of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/data presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag contributors who made figures/visual presentations as Visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Writing – original draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft (including substantive translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note typographic convention: role name uses an en dash; tag as 'Writing – original draft' and optionally set degree-contribution attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT role: Writing – review & editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision – including pre- or post-publication stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag as 'Writing – review & editing' (use en dash) for contributors who performed critical revision and editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility: CRediT tagging in JATS 1.1 and earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: JATS version 1.1 and earlier do not have @vocab* and @degree-contribution attributes; alternate attributes must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In JATS 1.1 use @content-type on <role> to hold the credit.niso.org URI and place the role name as text within <role>. Use @specific-use to hold degree-of-contribution values ('equal', 'lead', 'supporting') and include the degree in parenthesis within the role text if desired.
